proposals.evidence: DEDR5086 gives Tamil mēl/mēlukku/mēkku, Malayalam mēl/mēlē and Kannada mēga/mēle above, higher. These southern survey mel-/mēl-/mēk-/meg- spatial responses retain the attested lateral or velar extensions and ordinary locative endings of the high/above family. Source transcriptions are preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.

These southern pin-/pimp-/pih-/in(d)- survey responses retain the documented back/behind stem with ordinary locative extensions and regular Kannada-area loss of initial p/h. proposals.evidence: DEDR4449 gives the widespread southern pēn/pēnu louse family, including Kannada pēn, Malayalam pēn and Telugu pēnu. These survey pyānu/pēnə/yɛ̄ñu/ēnu forms retain the louse stem with ordinary final vowels or Kannada-area initial weakening; survey palatalization is preserved. This is a comparative family proposal; inheritance versus local transmission in this survey lect remains subject to review.
